title: HQARRF: Hierarchical Q-learning and Force-aware Routing for Multi-Charger Scheduling in Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks
abstract: arXiv:2609.13901v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-charger scheduling in wireless rechargeable sensor networks must weigh sensor death risk, charger energy, travel cost, return-to-base feasibility and inter-charger coordination at once, and schedulers driven by local urgency alone duplicate service and leave whole regions unattended. We present HQARRF, a two-level scheduler. Below, an interpretable ARR-F score ranks candidate clusters through an attraction term for local urgency, a repulsion term against charger crowding and a force bonus from nearby critical sensors. Above, adaptive zones compress regional state into a deadline-based risk estimate, and a gated Q-learning controller decides only whether to redirect service to a high-risk, under-served zone. Over 27 parameter points HQARRF attains the highest mean survival rate at 26, improving survival by 20.7 percentage points over the mean of five baselines and 9.2 over the strongest baseline at each point. translated_title: HQARRF：无线可充电传感器网络中多充电器调度的分层Q学习与力感知路由
translated_abstract: 无线可充电传感器网络中的多充电器调度必须同时权衡传感器死亡风险、充电器能量、行驶成本、返回基站的可行性以及充电器之间的协调，而仅由局部紧急性驱动的调度器会造成重复服务，并使整个区域无人照管。我们提出了HQARRF，一个两级调度器。在下层，可解释的ARR-F分数通过局部紧急性的吸引项、防止充电器拥挤的排斥项以及来自附近关键传感器的力加成项来对候选簇进行排序。在上层，自适应区域将区域状态压缩为基于截止时间的风险估计，门控Q学习控制器仅决定是否将服务重定向到高风险、服务不足的区域。在27个参数点上，HQARRF在26个点上取得了最高的平均存活率，相比五个基线的平均值将存活率提高了20.7个百分点，在每个点上相比最强基线提高了9.2个百分点。消融实验隔离了……
tldr: HQARRF提出分层调度框架：下层用可解释的ARR-F力感知评分（吸引、排斥与关键传感器力加成）排序候选充电簇，上层用门控Q学习控制器决定是否将服务重定向到高风险、服务不足的区域，在无线可充电传感器网络多充电器调度中将存活率相比最强基线提升9.2个百分点。
en_tdlr: HQARRF presents a two-level scheduler that combines a lower-level interpretable ARR-F force-aware score (attraction, repulsion, and critical-sensor force bonus) for ranking candidate clusters with an upper-level gated Q-learning controller deciding whether to redirect service to high-risk, under-served zones, improving survival rate by 9.2 percentage points over the strongest baseline in multi-charger scheduling for wireless rechargeable sensor networks.
